The implementation is solid. Here's a summary of what was done:

**Kernel design**: Uses `al.amdgpu.mfma_32x32x8_bf16_f32` — one wavefront (64 threads) per 32×32 output tile, with K-tiles of 16 BF16 processed as 2 MFMA steps. Global-to-shared loads use packed i32 vector views (16 bytes per load). Accumulation is FP32, output is BF16. B is transposed to (N, K) in the host wrapper to match the kernel's B^T memory layout.

**Results from [eval_result.json](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p02/round0/eval_result.json)**:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Compiled | true |
| Correctness | true (5/5) |
| Runtime | 1.99 ms |
| Reference | 0.232 ms |
| Max relative error | 0.78% |

The MFMA kernel is 5.2× faster than the earlier scalar version (10.3 ms) and passes correctness across all 5 randomized trials with well-controlled numerical error. The remaining gap to rocBLAS (8.6×) is expected for a single-wavefront-per-tile design without double buffering or larger composed block tiles.
